panels.description:
Total failed workflow executions the running n8n instances have recorded, summed over main, worker and webhook.
This is the raw counter, not increase(): a histogram series does not exist until its first observation, so a counter whose first sample is 1 has no 0->1 step and increase() reads it as 0. A workflow that failed once since the pod started would show as zero here otherwise.
Resets to 0 when a pod restarts.
panels.title: Failed Executions (since instance start)

panels.description:
Executions enqueued in Valkey and not yet picked up by a worker. A brief non-zero value is normal; N8nQueueBacklog alerts when it stays above zero for 15m, which means the worker is gone or cannot reach Valkey.
Reported by the main instance only.
panels.title: Queue Jobs Waiting

panels.description: Age of the most recent activity on any n8n instance. Scheduled workflows run several times a day, so a large value means the scheduler or the trigger registration is broken rather than a quiet day. N8nNoActivity alerts at 24h.
panels.title: Time Since Last Activity

panels.description:
Workflow executions completed per 5 minutes, split by outcome. Success is green and failure red because these are states, not series.
Covers every execution mode: trigger and manual on the main instance, integrated (sub-workflow) and error on the worker.
The first observation of a brand-new series is not visible to increase(); the Failed Executions tile reads the raw counter and is authoritative for whether anything has failed at all.
panels.title: Executions per 5m by Status

panels.description:
Failed executions per workflow since the instances started, with the name resolved from n8n_workflow_info (N8N_METRICS_INCLUDE_WORKFLOW_INFO), which the alerts cannot carry - the execution histogram labels only status, mode and workflow_id.
The or-fallback is deliberate: a bare group_left join drops any workflow with no info entry, which would hide a deleted workflow's failures entirely while the Failed Executions tile still counted them. A row with a blank Workflow is a workflow that no longer exists.
Counts reset when a pod restarts.
panels.title: Failed Executions by Workflow

targets.expr: (sum by (workflow_id) (n8n_workflow_execution_duration_seconds_count{status="failed"}) * on (workflow_id) group_left(workflow_name) n8n_workflow_info) or sum by (workflow_id) (n8n_workflow_execution_duration_seconds_count{status="failed"})

panels.description:
Executions started inside the dashboard window, read from execution_entity.
Unlike the Prometheus tiles above this survives a pod restart and covers everything n8n still keeps in Postgres, not just the life of the current process.
panels.title: Executions in Range

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "Executions"
FROM execution_entity e
WHERE e."deletedAt" IS NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(e."startedAt")
  AND e."workflowId" IN (${workflow:sqlstring})
  AND e.status IN (${status:sqlstring})

panels.description: Executions that ended in error or crashed. crashed means the process died mid-run (OOM kill, eviction) and n8n never wrote a result, so an error workflow never fires for those either.
panels.title: Failed in Range

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "Failed"
FROM execution_entity e
WHERE e."deletedAt" IS NULL
  AND e.status IN ('error', 'crashed')
  AND $__timeFilter(e."startedAt")
  AND e."workflowId" IN (${workflow:sqlstring})
  AND e.status IN (${status:sqlstring})

panels.description: Share of finished executions in range that succeeded. Runs still running or waiting are left out of both sides of the ratio, so a queue full of waiting runs does not drag this down.
panels.title: Success Rate

targets.rawSql:
SELECT round(
         100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.status = 'success')
         / NULLIF(count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.status IN ('success', 'error', 'crashed')), 0)
       , 1) AS "Success Rate"
FROM execution_entity e
WHERE e."deletedAt" IS NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(e."startedAt")
  AND e."workflowId" IN (${workflow:sqlstring})
  AND e.status IN (${status:sqlstring})

panels.description: 95th percentile of stoppedAt - startedAt over finished executions in range. Computed over the real rows, so it does not depend on the histogram buckets the n8n exporter happens to ship.
panels.title: P95 Duration

targets.rawSql:
SELECT round(percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (
         ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (e."stoppedAt" - e."startedAt"))
       )::numeric, 2) AS "P95"
FROM execution_entity e
WHERE e."deletedAt" IS NULL
  AND e."stoppedAt" IS NOT NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(e."startedAt")
  AND e."workflowId" IN (${workflow:sqlstring})
  AND e.status IN (${status:sqlstring})

panels.description:
Executions bucketed by start time and split by status.
This is the same shape as the Prometheus panel above but read from the table, so it keeps its history across pod restarts and covers statuses the exporter never labels, such as waiting and crashed.
panels.title: Executions by Status over Time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(e."startedAt", $__interval, 0),
  e.status AS metric,
  count(*) AS "executions"
FROM execution_entity e
WHERE e."deletedAt" IS NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(e."startedAt")
  AND e."workflowId" IN (${workflow:sqlstring})
  AND e.status IN (${status:sqlstring})
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.description:
One row per execution, newest first, for the workflows and statuses selected above.
Duration is stoppedAt - startedAt and is empty while a run is still going or parked on a Wait node. Queued is startedAt - createdAt, which is the time the job sat in Valkey before a worker picked it up; a growing Queued column means the worker is the bottleneck, not the workflow.
Payload is the execution data n8n stored for the run, JSON plus binary. Large values here are what fills the database.
Click an ID to open that execution in n8n. Capped at 500 rows.
panels.title: Executions

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  e.id                                                   AS "ID",
  e."startedAt"                                          AS "Started",
  COALESCE(w.name, e."workflowId")                       AS "Workflow",
  e.status                                               AS "Status",
  e.mode                                                 AS "Mode",
  EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (e."stoppedAt" - e."startedAt"))    AS "Duration",
  EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (e."startedAt" - e."createdAt"))    AS "Queued",
  e."jsonSizeBytes" + e."binaryDataSizeBytes"            AS "Payload",
  e."retryOf"                                            AS "Retry Of",
  e."waitTill"                                           AS "Wait Until",
  e."workflowId"                                         AS "WorkflowID"
FROM execution_entity e
LEFT JOIN workflow_entity w ON w.id = e."workflowId"
WHERE e."deletedAt" IS NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(e."startedAt")
  AND e."workflowId" IN (${workflow:sqlstring})
  AND e.status IN (${status:sqlstring})
ORDER BY e."startedAt" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 500

panels.description:
The same executions grouped by workflow, so a workflow that fails rarely but runs constantly is not hidden behind one that fails every time.
Success % counts only finished runs. Last Run is the newest start inside the window, not the newest overall.
panels.title: Executions by Workflow

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(w.name, e."workflowId")                                     AS "Workflow",
  count(*)                                                             AS "Executions",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.status IN ('error', 'crashed'))             AS "Failed",
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.status = 'success')
        / NULLIF(count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.status IN ('success', 'error', 'crashed')), 0), 1)
                                                                       AS "Success %",
  round(avg(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (e."stoppedAt" - e."startedAt")))::numeric, 2) AS "Avg Duration",
  round(max(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (e."stoppedAt" - e."startedAt")))::numeric, 2) AS "Max Duration",
  sum(e."jsonSizeBytes" + e."binaryDataSizeBytes")                     AS "Payload",
  max(e."startedAt")                                                   AS "Last Run"
FROM execution_entity e
LEFT JOIN workflow_entity w ON w.id = e."workflowId"
WHERE e."deletedAt" IS NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(e."startedAt")
  AND e."workflowId" IN (${workflow:sqlstring})
  AND e.status IN (${status:sqlstring})
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY "Failed" DESC, "Executions" DESC

panels.description:
Displays the actual physical memory (RAM) used by the n8n process (Resident Set Size).
This is the most critical indicator of real memory pressure on the host.
panels.title: Resident Memory Usage (RSS)

panels.description:
Shows the total count of all active libuv handles currently managed by Node.js.
High or increasing values over time might suggest resource exhaustion or unexpected behavior in your application.
panels.title: Total Active Handles

panels.description:
Shows the current event loop lag in seconds.

This value reflects the real-time delay in the Node.js event loop.  
A consistently high value suggests the system is struggling to process events timely, possibly due to heavy synchronous tasks or CPU bottlenecks.
panels.title: Current Event Loop Lag

panels.description:
Displays the Total CPU usage (user + system) of the n8n process over time.

Uses the Prometheus metric n8n_process_cpu_seconds_total with rate() over 5 minutes to show the CPU consumption rate per second.

Values are shown as CPU seconds used per second, which is automatically formatted in milliseconds (ms) for readability.

Interpretation:

1 s/s = 100% of a single core

0.5 s/s = 50% of a single core

0.01 s/s = 1% of a single core

This visualization does NOT adjust for the number of CPU cores; it's raw usage on a single-core equivalent.
panels.title: Total CPU Usage (User + System) Rate 5m

panels.description:
Shows the Resident Memory (RSS) and Virtual Memory of the n8n process over time.
- Resident Memory (Green): Actual physical RAM used by the process.
- Virtual Memory (Yellow): Total allocated address space (can be much larger than physical usage).
Unit: IEC (GiB, MiB) to match OS-level memory reporting.
panels.title: Resident vs Virtual Memory

panels.description:
Displays the Event Loop Lag over time using three key metrics:
- **Mean (average):** The average delay of the event loop over the collection window.
- **Max:** The maximum recorded delay, showing peak lag spikes.
- **P99:** The 99th percentile, indicating the worst lag observed for 99% of the time.

These metrics help detect event loop blocking patterns, monitor performance trends, and identify rare but impactful latency spikes.
panels.title: Event Loop Lag - Mean, Max, P99

panels.description:
Description:
Tracks the Node.js heap memory usage over time.

Used Heap: Actual memory used for objects.

Total Heap: Allocated heap limit.
Memory is reported in bytes and auto-scaled (MB, GB) for readability.
A sudden increase in total heap may indicate memory pressure, increased load, or recent workload spikes.
panels.title: Heap Usage - Used vs Total

panels.description:
Displays Node.js heap space memory usage broken down by space type.
Shows memory consumption in each segment like 'old', 'new', 'large object', 'code', and others.
Helps identify inefficient memory usage or potential memory leaks in specific heap spaces.
panels.title: Heap Space Usage by Type

panels.description:
Displays the average time spent in Garbage Collection (GC) over the past 5 minutes, broken down by type (minor, major, incremental).
The values are calculated as rate over time (rate()), giving the average GC pause time per second in the selected time range.

Minor GC: Quick cleanup of short-lived objects (frequent, low duration).

Major GC: Full heap cleanup of long-lived objects (rare, high impact).

Incremental GC: Partial cleanup to reduce long pauses (intermediate).

This panel helps monitor how much of your Node.js process time is being spent in GC activity and highlights GC pressure trends over time.
panels.title: GC Duration (Minor, Major, Incremental) - Rate over 5m

panels.description:
Displays the current number of active Node.js libuv handles grouped by type (e.g., Socket, Server).

Each handle type represents an underlying C++ class (e.g., TCP Socket, Timer, Pipe).

This can help diagnose resource leaks, stalled connections, or unexpected handle growth over time.
panels.title: Active Handles by Type

panels.description:
Shows the current number of active asynchronous resources that are keeping the Node.js event loop alive, grouped by resource type (e.g., PipeWrap, TCPSocketWrap, Timeout).
These represent internal Node.js resources tied to async operations like timers, sockets, and pipes.
An unexpected increase or steady accumulation of certain resource types may indicate stuck or inefficient asynchronous code (e.g., open sockets not closing, long-running timers).
panels.title: Active Resources by Type

list.definition: SELECT w.name AS "__text", w.id AS "__value" FROM workflow_entity w ORDER BY 1
list.description: Workflows to include. Values are workflow IDs so a rename does not break a saved selection.
list.label: Workflow
list.name: workflow
list.query: SELECT w.name AS "__text", w.id AS "__value" FROM workflow_entity w ORDER BY 1

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT status FROM execution_entity WHERE "deletedAt" IS NULL ORDER BY 1
list.description: Execution statuses to include. Only statuses n8n has actually recorded are listed.
list.label: Status
list.name: status
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT status FROM execution_entity WHERE "deletedAt" IS NULL ORDER BY 1

list.description: Base URL the ID column links to. The dashboard is a static file, so the gateway hostname cannot be templated in and lives here instead.
list.label: n8n URL
list.name: n8n_url
